a test of conscience.text: Some films end on a choice, the moment a person must weigh what they want against what is right. The potter Genjūrō, [drawn into marriage by Lady Wakasa|1953-ugetsu] while his wife waits on the shore, can only be loosened from her hold by a priest who paints sacred symbols on his body. In Tumbbad, Vinayak [returns fifteen years later hungry for the hidden treasure|2018-tumbbad] and lowers himself on a rope to steal gold from a starving god. Six of the record's ten films with this ending come from Asia, among them Jigoku (1960) and The Medium (2021).

dying to save others.text: The oldest consolation horror offers is that one life, freely given, can buy back the rest. In Wisborg, [Ellen reads that only a pure-hearted woman's blood, freely given, can hold Count Orlok|1922-nosferatu] as the town fills with deaths. In Georgetown, [Father Damien Karras, a priest losing his faith|1973-the-exorcist], answers a girl whose stomach spells out the words 'help me', and on the express to Busan [Seok-woo, a cynical workaholic, travels with his young daughter Su-an|2016-train-to-busan] as the dead surge through the carriages. The ending runs through every era of the record, from Nosferatu to A Quiet Place (2018).

everyone dies.text: The bleakest ending leaves no one to carry the story out. Liza Merrill [reopens a New Orleans hotel that stands over one of the seven gates of hell|1981-the-beyond], and soon the dead begin to walk. At a lakefront holiday home, [two polite young men bet that none of the family will live until morning|1997-funny-games], and in Siccin [a spell promises death to Nisa and everyone of her blood|2014-siccin] once five night prayers have passed. No film in the record ends this way before 1960, and it is about twice as common in continental Europe as in North America.

getting out alive.text: Sometimes the ending asks nothing more than that someone makes it to morning. In Haddonfield, [Laurie Strode is shadowed through Halloween by a man in a white mask|1978-halloween] while her friends laugh off her fears. Grace, [hunted from room to room by her new in-laws on her wedding night|2019-ready-or-not], has only until dawn, and in Tehran [Shideh and her daughter Dorsa are left alone in their apartment|2016-under-the-shadow] as missiles fall and the neighbours flee. Since 2015 about one film in six in the record ends with someone simply getting out.

it was never real.text: Some films pull the floor away at the end and leave the haunting with an ordinary explanation. In an abandoned palace in Allahabad, [a woman's singing draws Hari Shankar through the empty rooms|1949-mahal], and in Chandanghat [Kumar scoffs at warnings of a vengeful spirit|1962-bees-saal-baad] until a man wearing his stolen coat dies beneath the tree where his father and grandfather were killed. Professor Philip Goodman, who [built a television career debunking fraudulent psychics|2017-ghost-stories], is handed three cases to solve. Three of the record's eleven such endings come from South Asia, a high share for a region with sixteen films.

killing someone close.text: The cruellest ending turns a person's hand against the ones they love most. In Cincinnati, [Martin calmly demands that the surgeon Steven give up a life from his own family|2017-the-killing-of-a-sacred-deer], and until Steven chooses, his children lose the use of their legs and refuse food. In a remote house in the woods [Leah summons a demon to kill her mother, then regrets it as the two grow close again|2017-pyewacket]. The ending reaches back to The Wolf Man (1941), and ten of its fourteen films were made since 2000.

living alongside the uncanny.text: Some films end with a truce, the living and the uncanny settling into the same house. In a Stockholm suburb, [Oskar taps coded messages through the wall to Eli|2008-let-the-right-one-in], the strange child next door who needs blood. In Adelaide, [Amelia raises Sam in the shadow of the Mister Babadook book|2014-the-babadook], and [a goddess lies bound in tree roots in a barn on a Welsh island|2018-apostle], fed on blood, while Thomas Richardson searches for his sister. Eight of the record's thirteen such endings come from films made between 2000 and 2014.

loved ones reunited.text: Some endings bring the lost back together, whether the meeting happens in life or beyond it. The potter Genjūrō, [drawn away from his wife Miyagi by the noblewoman Lady Wakasa|1953-ugetsu], at last takes the road home. In Dakar, [Ada is promised to the wealthy Omar while her lover Souleiman sets out across the sea|2019-atlantics], and the lost men return at night inside the bodies of the living. In Spain, [Laura searches for months after Simón disappears|2007-the-orphanage] from the orphanage where she grew up.

surviving at terrible cost.text: Some survivors walk out of the story carrying more than they can hold. At Appleyard College, [only Irma is found after the climb up Hanging Rock|1975-picnic-at-hanging-rock], with no memory of what happened. In Seoul, [Gang-du is quarantined with his family|2006-the-host] while his daughter phones from the sewers where the monster keeps its prey, and in Kwaidan [a young woodcutter is spared by a snow spirit|1964-kwaidan] on condition that he never speaks of that night. No film in the record ends this way before 1960, and nearly two thirds of these endings come from 2000 onward.

taken to the other side.text: The worst endings carry a person off, to a place or a loop they can never leave. In Dead of Night, [Walter Craig's recurring dream ends in something awful|1945-dead-of-night], and [Eleanor Lance, lonely and guilty, comes to stay at Hill House|1963-the-haunting], where the doors close on their own. Liza Merrill [reopens a New Orleans hotel built over one of the seven gates of hell|1981-the-beyond]. The ending is spread almost evenly across the decades since 1960, and British and European films account for nearly half of it.

the dead find peace.text: The gentlest ending in horror lets the dead stop wanting. In Antonio Bay, [the drowned crew of the Elizabeth Dane roll in with the fog|1980-the-fog], a century after the town's founders wrecked their ship. In Philadelphia, [Cole Sear confides that he sees dead people|1999-the-sixth-sense], and Malcolm urges him to learn what the ghosts need from him, and in Chanderi [townsfolk paint O Stree Kal Aana on their walls|2018-stree] to keep a woman's spirit moving on. Twelve of these twenty films come from Asia, and the ending was most common in the 1980s and 90s.

the ending is left open.text: Some films stop at the edge of an answer and leave the viewer standing there. On Valentine's Day 1900, [three schoolgirls walk in a trance into a crevice of Hanging Rock|1975-picnic-at-hanging-rock], and in Antarctica [MacReady takes command, trusting no one|1982-the-thing], once the radio is smashed and the blood destroyed. In Paris, [an unknown sender keeps texting Maureen|2016-personal-shopper] until a body on a bloodied bathroom floor leaves her unsure. Open endings have nearly tripled since the record's earliest films, and British and European films leave them open about twice as often as North American ones.

the evil is cast out.text: Some threats cannot be killed, only driven back through the door they came in by. In a Rhode Island farmhouse where every clock stops at 3:07, [Ed and Lorraine Warren learn the land bears a witch's curse|2013-the-conjuring] as a spirit takes hold of Carolyn Perron. In Derry, [the Losers Club follow the sewer maps to an old well|2017-it] beneath a house on Neibolt Street, and in Adelaide [Amelia tears up the Mister Babadook book and finds it back on her doorstep|2014-the-babadook]. Close to two thirds of these endings come from North American films.

the evil is destroyed.text: The oldest promise in horror is that the monster can be killed and the lights turned back on. Ellen Ripley [returns to LV-426 with the Colonial Marines|1986-aliens] and finds a frightened girl named Newt, the only colonist left. In Santa Carla, [Michael begins to shun the light after drinking from a bottle of blood|1987-the-lost-boys], and in the outback [Carl is chased through the night by wild pigs|1984-razorback] as he searches for his missing wife. Half the record's films before 1960 end with the evil destroyed; between 2000 and 2014 fewer than one in five do.

the evil is handed on.text: Some evils survive by changing hands, and the ending only passes the curse along. In Ringu, [Reiko Asakawa watches the tape, the phone screeches, and her seven days begin|1998-ringu]. Joy Ramirez [hangs a found bagua mirror at her front door for luck|2004-feng-shui], and it takes a soul for every stroke of good fortune, and in Coming Soon [an actress's safety sling snaps on the last take of a hanging scene|2008-coming-soon], and that take is in the released film. None of these endings appear in the record before 1960, and nearly three quarters come from 2000 onward.

the evil lives on.text: The most common ending in the record denies the audience its relief, leaving the evil still out there when the lights come up. In Haddonfield, [Michael Myers moves from house to house along Laurie's street|1978-halloween] after dark. In Black Christmas [the calls are coming from inside the sorority house|1974-black-christmas], and in Gokseong [Jong-goo finds his daughter's shoe in the stranger's shrine|2016-the-wailing] as she falls ill herself. Fewer than one in five films before 1960 let the threat endure; since 2015 a third do.

the evil spreads.text: The widest ending lets the threat slip past the story and into the world beyond it. In South Africa's Tsitsikamma forest, the forestry worker [Gabi is nursed by Barend and his son Stefan|2021-gaia], while fungus-covered people stalk the house at night and mushrooms sprout from living flesh. The record holds this ending from Shivers (1975), where [a kiss passes parasites from apartment to apartment|1975-shivers], to Pulse (2001), where [friends in Tokyo fade into stains on the wall|2001-pulse-kairo], and in none made before 1960.

the guilty are punished.text: Some endings settle the account, when justice, revenge or a curse turned back finds the one who earned it. On Dr. Moreau's island, [the beast-men chant his Law and scatter at the crack of his whip|1932-island-of-lost-souls]. Grace is [hunted from room to room by in-laws sure they must sacrifice her before dawn|2019-ready-or-not], and in Guatemala [protesters trap the former dictator Enrique Monteverde in his house|2019-la-llorona] while a new maid teaches his granddaughter to hold her breath under water. The ending appears in about one film in ten, and was most common before 1960.

the hidden truth comes out.text: Some endings turn the whole story on its axis, so that everything seen before must be seen again. On the island of Jersey in 1945, [Grace Stewart keeps her house in darkness for her children|2001-the-others] and comes to believe it is haunted. In Philadelphia, [Malcolm Crowe takes on the frightened boy Cole Sear|1999-the-sixth-sense] after a former patient shoots him, and in a secluded country house [Su-mi blames her stepmother for the bruises on her sister's arms|2003-a-tale-of-two-sisters]. The twist ending peaked in the record's films of the 1980s and 90s.

the place is destroyed.text: Sometimes the ending tears down the place itself, the walls that held the horror. At a Freiburg dance academy, [Suzy Bannion learns that a coven dies with its leader|1977-suspiria]. A poet's young wife [glimpses a heart beating inside the walls of the house she is restoring|2017-mother], until a crowd of admirers tears the home apart, and on a Welsh island [three founders swear that blood sacrifice made the barren soil fertile|2018-apostle]. The record finds this ending in no film made between 2000 and 2014.

the protagonist dies.text: Some films let their central figure die, with nothing saved by it. In Venice, [John Baxter keeps glimpsing a small figure in a red coat|1973-don-t-look-now] and scoffs at the warning that he must leave. Eleanor Lance [comes to Hill House lonely and guilty|1963-the-haunting], and in Francoist Spain [a faun hails Ofelia as a lost princess of the underworld|2006-pan-s-labyrinth] and sets her three tasks. The ending was common before 1960 and almost vanished in the 1980s and 90s, when only three films in the record used it.

the story survives.text: Some films end on what remains to be told: a memory, a piece of proof, a warning handed down. In a secluded country house, [Su-mi comes home from a mental institution|2003-a-tale-of-two-sisters] to a stepmother she blames and a wardrobe that frightens her sister. On their California ranch, OJ and Em Haywood [set out to catch the thing in the cloud on camera|2022-nope] and sell the shot. Older films such as Häxan (1922) and The Housemaid (1960) end the same way, and none from the 1980s or 90s do.

the truth is buried.text: Some endings leave the truth in the dark, denied, disbelieved or pinned on the wrong person. In a sorority house at Christmas, [the police shrug off the missing|1974-black-christmas] while the sisters are killed one by one upstairs. In Siccin, [Öznur turns to black magic to make her cousin Kudret hers|2014-siccin], and the spell sets jinn upon his wife Nisa. The record finds this ending from Häxan (1922) and The Wolf Man (1941) to Trollhunter (2010) and Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum (2018), and it was most common before 1960.

things are set right.text: Some endings undo the harm: the child comes back, the family is whole, the morning is clear. In Georgetown, [Regan MacNeil's bed shakes and she speaks in a voice that is not hers|1973-the-exorcist]. Ellen Ripley [finds a frightened girl named Newt, the only colonist left|1986-aliens] on LV-426, and in apartment 13B [Manu alone sees that what happens to a family on channel 13 soon happens to his own|2009-13b]. South Asian films reach for this ending most readily, nearly a third of them.

victims become the evil.text: The cruellest turn in horror comes when the one we feared for becomes the thing we fear. In 1630s New England, [grief and hunger turn a family's suspicion toward their daughter Thomasin|2015-the-witch] while the twins insist their goat Black Phillip talks to them. In Utah, [Annie Graham learns a séance from a kindly woman at a support group|2018-hereditary], and in Bali [the anthropologist Cathy Kean flies off as a severed head to devour an unborn baby|1981-mystics-in-bali]. Barely one film in twenty ends this way before 1960; from the 1960s on it is one in six or seven.
